title: Balancing Academic Rigour Required to Excel at PSLE With Skills to Thrive in AI-driven Economy
what_it_is: Balancing Academic Rigour Required to Excel at PSLE With Skills to Thrive in AI-driven Economy

sections.label: PSLE rigour and learning approaches
sections.summary: The Ministry states PSLE assesses core concepts and critical thinking, not rote learning, and schools use inquiry-based, collaborative and experiential learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry considers that the academic rigour required to excel in the PSLE, such as rote memorisation and test-taking abilities (i) reflects the skills our youths need to thrive in the AI-driven economy, (ii) nurtures a lifelong love of learning and (iii) compares favourably with inquiry-based and collaborative learning approaches more common in other internationally recognised primary school curricula.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: It is designed to assess core concepts and skills in the primary school curriculum, including the ability to think critically and apply concepts in different contexts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: PSLE does not emphasise rote learning or test-taking skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: To prepare students for the future, schools also design co-curricular programmes, applied learning programmes, Character and Citizenship Education lessons and leadership opportunities to nurture students' 21st Century Competencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Our teachers use a range of pedagogies, such as inquiry-based, collaborative and experiential learning, to facilitate students' learning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: We are heartened that international benchmarking studies, like the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study, have found that our primary school students are adept in reasoning, and applying concepts and skills to navigate non-routine situations and solve more complex problems.

sections.label: Collaboration and inquiry-based learning training
sections.summary: Collaboration and inquiry-based learning is integrated into all schools, with educators trained in these core skillsets at the National Institute of Education.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, collaboration and inquiry-based learning is integrated into all of the schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This is something that our professionals as part of their training in the National Institute of Education, whether they are doing it as part of their original practicum or they go on to become specialists in particular areas of education.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These are core skillsets for our educators and they integrate them into the curriculum, into the syllabus on a regular basis; and they do so for every school and they give every child the opportunity to do so.

sections.label: Educators reviewing other education systems
sections.summary: The answer is yes, educators regularly and consistently look at other education systems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The short answer is yes, our educators are regularly and consistently looking at other education systems.
